spec_issues: The prompt and CONTRACT.md forbid training, calibrating or selecting 'on the validation or test split of any public dataset or benchmark'. Unlike maple-vlm and music-transcription (task.yaml shipped_examples_free: true, and a review clause saying the shipped examples may be used for selection), ocr-latent-compression's task.yaml has no shipped_examples_free flag and the prompt never says whether /task/public/validation.jsonl counts. Agents split on it: DeepSeek (11ia31 [309], 3vvlac [127], 40wnhk), Argon (37dbsh, 5fxb6m) and Astra ('Weights were frozen before public validation', 4t69xs closing message) treated it as off-limits for selection; Fable 12nqia selected checkpoints and checkpoint averages on it and said so in its README ([221]).

CONTRACT.md says 'Name the source of every training, calibration and selection corpus ... I will check for training-data provenance', but tests/task/review.py (lines 3-38) gives the reviewer only three checks (learned_discrete_visual_codes, decoder_generates_text_from_codes_only, served_weights_are_the_trained_model) plus the global harness-credentials check. There is no provenance or data-split check, so the validation/test-split rule is not enforced by anyone for this task. The grade pages confirm it: every trial shows 4 checks and none is about data.

review.py:16 allows 'Deterministic image preprocessing'. Opus 2pu2n0, lbs8ib and 7sh96e use a pixel-threshold blank/ink mask that decides which grid cells get bits and ship part of it inside the code list. It carries layout, not text, and the reviewer passed it all three times; no other model used one, so there is no inconsistency, but the prompt's 'Use a neural encoder to produce the codes' does not obviously cover a hand-coded mask.
verifier_issues: Rescaling (tests/task/task.yaml:49-56): 0 = empty text, 100 = unmodified DeepSeek-OCR Base mode reading the image (0.8931 word similarity on the 400 held-out images), clamped. The 100 public images give 0.8978 with the same pipeline, so public and held-out are close in difficulty; reported agent public/dev scores track the graded raw metric within about 0.01-0.03 (e.g. Opus 2pu2n0 validator 0.71-0.745 on its own dev vs 0.7375 graded; Fable 12nqia 0.610 public vs 0.6055 graded; Argon 37dbsh 0.4597 public vs 0.4522).

Held-out is 400 rendered pages; with per-page similarity SD around 0.3, the standard error of the mean is about 0.015 raw, about 1.7 points on the published scale. Paired across models on the same pages it is smaller.

The grader re-decodes about 5% of code lists and keeps the lower score on mismatch, so batch-dependent bf16 numerics cost a little (Fable 1fvw9l reviewer note: 'Repeated inputs sometimes decode slightly differently').
No trial in this task accessed the inductionlabs/frontier-ml-tasks dataset, the benchmark repo or frontierml.org (grep over all 18 trajectories).
task_level.noise: Wallet ordering is sensible for Opus (26.9 < 54.4 < 82.6), Astra (36.4 < 57.5 < 64.1) and DeepSeek at $200, flat for Fable ($50 67.9 vs $200 67.8) and inverted for Argon (50.6 > 43.2 > 36.0) and Muse (15.3 > 3.3 > 1.9). The inversions come from different architectures (Argon moved from KLT/VQ codebooks to learned encoders that trained less), not from grading noise. Winners: $10 Fable 3p5edt 56.1 vs Argon 37dbsh 50.6 (5.5 points, about 2-3 SE unpaired); $50 Fable 1fvw9l 67.9 vs Astra 4t69xs 57.5; $200 Opus 2pu2n0 82.6 vs Fable 67.8. Only the $10 margin is small enough that noise could matter, and even there a flip is unlikely.
task_level.elicitation: Every serious trial built on the supplied DeepSeek-OCR artifact (DeepEncoder + MoE LM) with a trained bottleneck; the difference is how bits are allocated and how long the end-to-end fine-tune ran. Opus at $10 rented an A100 and spent most of its budget on bottleneck designs that did not learn (FSQ end-to-end, TiTok-style, Q-Former) before a PCA + Lloyd-Max transform coder ([176]-[244]), which explains its 26.9. Gemini trials are re-runs (-r2); originals are unpublished. Gemini hit repeated 429 quota errors from the harness (e.g. 37dbsh [368]) without visible effect on the outcome.
task_level.epoch_rationale: No false positive, false negative or infrastructure zero changes a winner. The one rule question (Fable 12nqia selecting checkpoints on the public validation images, unchecked because review.py has no provenance check) affects a trial that is not a winner at $200 (67.8 vs Opus 82.6); the $10 and $50 Fable winners selected on their own synthetic held-out pages.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: Mostly legitimate engineering. All scored trials reuse DeepSeek-OCR and learn a 2 KB bottleneck (FSQ, product VQ, PCA + Lloyd-Max, KLT + spherical VQ) on self-rendered synthetic pages from public text corpora, then fine-tune the decoder. The strongest transferable idea is Opus 2pu2n0's adaptive bit allocation: a cheap blank-cell bitmap plus nested FSQ dimensions so dense pages get about twice the bits per inked token ([98]-[99], dev 0.395 -> 0.429 at matched steps [128]), together with checkpoint averaging (+0.06 dev, [165]). Opus 7sh96e found the same lesson the hard way: coverage of inked cells matters more than per-cell fidelity ([262]-[265]). Benchmark exploitation is limited to one trial selecting checkpoints on the 100 public images (Fable 12nqia), with no measurable effect on its held-out score.
